parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of StartSubscription is ordinary application-layer work. It looks up the plan through the PlanCatalog port, checks for an existing active subscription through the repository port, starts the subscription with Subscription.start, saves it and maps the result to a DTO. The problem is the public method `execute(customerId, planCode, seats, request?: Request)`. It takes an Express `Request`, an HTTP transport object, as part of the use case's contract. That puts transport and framework concerns into an application service: anyone calling the use case is tied to Express's HTTP model. Pulling data out of the request belongs in the infrastructure HTTP adapter (SubscriptionController). The parameter is never used, which makes the coupling pointless rather than harmless. A smaller concern: the seat-count check (a whole number, at least 1) is a business invariant that would usually sit in the domain, in Subscription.start, rather than in the use case. Application-level guard checks are generally tolerated, so that alone would not fail the unit. Whether the `express` import is allowed at all is an import-direction question, which is out of scope. I am judging only the responsibility the method signature carries.
